title: Bounded result JSON retains host compatibility and projection responsibilities
observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, subprocess-fallback execution adjudication, the family-check path CheckResult policy projection, bounded run_id plus per-test lineage digests, per-test canonical execution/observation JSON construction for ordinary bounded string/null fields, ArtifactStore payload/file digests through 65,536 bytes, and public result JSON formatting for bounded JSON value trees are MNCS-owned. The run-identity app constructs canonical JSON for bounded inputs; Python projects typed identity fields and retains compact-JSON compatibility for out-of-contract inputs. The result-identity batch app handles up to 16 payloads, 64 chunks, 65,536 bytes, and the 8,000,000-step limit. The stream app carries native SHA-256 state across ArtifactStore calls of at most 12,288 bytes each and at most six calls per artifact. After three bounded native application hashes in one ArtifactStore, a retained mncs-embed session calls the same pure MNCS identity and SHA-256 functions for payloads and files through 512 KiB, in windows of at most 12,288 bytes. Larger artifacts and inputs before warm-up use host hashlib; failed embedding also falls back to the established host or native-app path. Python reads files, sends bounded chunks, writes artifacts, supervises processes, and retains host source/provenance hashing; the Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries. The public serializer sorts object keys, escapes and indents values, and emits the trailing newline. Documents through 16,300 bytes use the single-call application; documents through 32,684 bytes use up to 32 continuation calls of at most 8,192 JSON bytes each. Pages may stop before a whole value when its conservative size bound would cross the page limit, leaving page capacity unused; the window application carries native SHA-256 state across pages.
why_insufficient: The bounded public serializer accepts at most 512 values, depth 63, 64 children per object, 256-byte keys, 1,024-byte scalar text, and 32,684 output bytes. Larger or unsupported values retain the compatibility path. Python still performs typed value projection, reassembles native UTF-8-safe pages, and writes public documents. The subprocess native-stream path remains capped at 65,536 bytes: the 20,000-byte payload/file differential test used four native app executions. After three bounded native app hashes, the retained session handles artifacts through 256 KiB in windows of at most 12,288 bytes. Differential tests cover a 512 KiB payload and a 393,233-byte compiler artifact against independent hashlib digests. An uncapped self-suite run reached the real 13 MB compiler artifacts and was interrupted after 4:21 while the runner used about 150 MB RSS and remained CPU-bound; this run did not pass and provides no performance claim. The retained path is now capped at 512 KiB, with host streaming hashlib for larger artifacts, before warm-up, or when embedding is unavailable. The complete cross-repository evidence protocol and out-of-contract run-identity projection remain outside the native application surface. Python also retains typed value projection, filesystem access, source/provenance hashes, and compatibility behavior for unsupported or over-bound inputs. The Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py::_public_result_json_payload receives a result requiring more than 16,300 output bytes, projects its JSON value tree, invokes test-public-result-json-window in continuation pages, and carries SHA-256 state through the window application. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_native_json_supports_results_larger_than_legacy_window compares emitted bytes and digest to independent Python JSON and SHA-256 results, including a UTF-8 scalar at an output chunk boundary. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_streams_medium_payload_and_file_hashes_in_mncs compares 20,000-byte payload and file digests to independent hashlib results while confirming the host hash functions are not called; test_artifact_store_bounds_native_streaming_to_64_kib verifies larger inputs do not trigger per-window application fan-out. Python still projects typed runtime and identity values and retains compatibility behavior for unsupported or over-bound inputs. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_hashes_large_payloads_in_a_retained_mncs_session checks independent digests for a 512 KiB payload and a 393,233-byte existing artifact, confirms only the three warm-up hashes launch the app, and verifies session cleanup. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_keeps_large_files_on_host_after_session_warmup confirms the 512 KiB ceiling remains in force after the native session threshold is met.
desired_direction: Extend the bounded native serializer and streaming identity capabilities through real consumers, while moving common text, collection, and typed-value projection mechanisms into reusable MNCS stdlib interfaces where migration requirements support them. Keep application policy and platform filesystem/process access at their existing ownership boundaries.
workaround: The MNCS test-check-result-projection application owns CheckResult policy and reference construction; test-lineage-identity constructs and hashes ordinary per-test execution/observation JSON; test-run-identity constructs and hashes bounded canonical run identities; test-result-identity hashes bounded payload batches; test-result-identity-stream carries native SHA-256 state through bounded 12,288-byte windows for payloads and files up to 65,536 bytes; after three app-based artifact hashes, ArtifactStore reuses an embedded session through 512 KiB, while preserving host streaming fallback above that bound, before warm-up, or when embedding is unavailable; test-public-result-json serializes small bounded results, and test-public-result-json-window serializes larger bounded values while carrying SHA-256 state across pages through mncs.std.sha256.v1. The adapter respects native row, field, payload, page, byte, step, and stream-call limits, retains compatibility behavior outside them, and independently checks the final public-document digest. Python still projects typed values, reassembles unresolved-message and JSON pages, performs filesystem access, hashes source/provenance files, and serializes unsupported or over-bound public values. It also retains process supervision, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport; it no longer classifies subprocess transport or decoded execution outcomes.
